# Agent terminals on a project

## What to build

An agent terminal (or a plain one) can be opened **on a project**: the agent then works in the project folder `<workspacesDir>/.projects/<id>/` and sees every repo of the project through `repos/<name>` (spec goal **MR-02**, section "graph-manager: terminals and tools (MR-02)", first bullet).

What already exists (in this codebase, before this task):
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/projects.ts` exports `PROJECTS_DIR = ".projects"`, `PROJECT_FILE = "project.json"`, `interface Project { id: string; name: string; workspaces: string[]; createdAt: string }`, `projectDirOf(workspacesDir, id)` (absolute `<workspacesDir>/.projects/<id>`), `createProjectFolder`, `syncProjectFolder`, `removeProjectFolder`, `repoNamesOf`. The project folder is a git repo with `project.json`, `.gitignore` (`repos/`, `.graph-execution/`), `repos/<name>` links and a first commit; it has a git identity (a local one is set when none is configured).
- `DataStore` (`src/server/store.ts`) has `projects: Record<id, { name, workspaces, createdAt }>` in its data and the readers `store.projects(): Project[]` and `store.project(id): Project | undefined`.
- `src/server/routes/projects.ts` serves `GET/POST/PATCH/DELETE /api/projects`; `GET` answers `{ projects: ProjectView[] }` with `ProjectView = { id, name, forge, path, createdAt, workspaces: { id, fullPath, repo }[] }`. Its DELETE closes terminals whose `cwd` is inside the project folder, then removes the folder.
- `src/web/types.ts` has `ProjectEntry` (the same shape as `ProjectView`); `src/web/pages/Projects.tsx` lists projects in a `pj-table` whose last cell (`.pj-actions` or similar flex row) holds **Edit repos** and a delete button; `src/server/liverun.ts` exports `liveRunIn(ctx, { id, path })`.
Read those files first; names may differ slightly — follow what is there.

This task adds:
1. `POST /api/terminals { projectId }` (instead of `workspaceId`): cwd = the project folder, title = the project name (`<Agent label> · <project name>` for an agent), env `GM_PROJECT_ID=<id>`, and `TerminalInfo.projectId`. Agent buttons work with it, including Qwen Code, whose committed `.qwen/settings.json` goes into the project folder's own git repo (never into a workspace).
2. The Terminals page: a sidebar section per project, the project in the New terminal dialog, and `/terminals?project=<id>[&agent=<agentId>]` opening a terminal there once.
3. The Projects page: the agent buttons (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Qwen Code, plus a plain terminal) on each project row.

NOT in this task: `open_start_run` from a project terminal and anything about runs of a project (`project~<id>`, Start run drawer for a project, `RunSummary.project`) — a later task does that and will read `TerminalInfo.projectId` / `GM_PROJECT_ID`, so set both exactly as named here. Do not change `src/server/tools/*` or `routes/internal.ts`.

- `apps/graph-manager/src/web/pages/Terminals.test.tsx` (lines 64–125 `AGENTS`, `serve()` fetch mock — unknown URLs answer 404; 348–355 the `?workspace=` StrictMode test; 477–516 agent button and Qwen tests).

## Patterns to follow

Server, in `POST /api/terminals` (`routes/terminals.ts`):
```ts
const createBody = z.object({
  workspaceId: z.string().min(1).optional(),
  projectId: z.string().min(1).optional(),
  cwd: ..., title: ..., cols: ..., rows: ..., agent: z.enum(AGENT_IDS).optional(),
}).strict();
...
if (body.workspaceId !== undefined && body.projectId !== undefined) return reply.code(400).send({ error: "pass workspaceId or projectId, not both" });
let project: Project | undefined;
if (body.projectId !== undefined) {
  project = ctx.store.project(body.projectId);
  if (!project) return reply.code(404).send({ error: "project not found" });
  cwd = projectDirOf(config.workspacesDir, project.id);
  if (!existsSync(path.join(cwd, PROJECT_FILE))) return reply.code(404).send({ error: "project folder is missing" });
}
const projectEnv = project ? { GM_PROJECT_ID: project.id } : undefined;
```
Title: plain terminal `body.title?.trim() || project.name`; agent `body.title?.trim() || \`${adapter.label} · ${project.name}\`` (the existing workspace rule, line 72, uses the repo name the same way). Pass `projectId: project?.id` and `env: { ...launch.env, ...projectEnv }` (plain: `env: projectEnv`) to `terminals.create`.

Qwen (`project-config`): `prepareProjectConfig(adapter, ws ?? { path: cwd })` when a workspace or a project is given; keep the existing 400 text `Qwen Code needs a workspace` when neither is (the existing test asserts it). Change the parameter of `prepareProjectConfig` to `target: { path: string }` (a `Workspace` still fits) and update its doc comment ("the workspace or project folder").

`TerminalInfo` / `CreateTerminal` / `Term` (`terminals.ts`): add `projectId?: string` next to `workspaceId`, copy it in `create`, and in `info()` add `...(t.projectId ? { projectId: t.projectId } : {})`. Add `"GM_PROJECT_ID"` to `STRIPPED_ENV` (line 99) so a graph-manager started from a project terminal does not pass its parent's id on.

Web: an id-param effect like the `?workspace=` one (Terminals.tsx:257–274, StrictMode-safe through a `handled` ref):
```ts
const projectParam = params.get("project");
const agentParam = params.get("agent");
useEffect(() => {
  const key = projectParam ? `${projectParam}:${agentParam ?? ""}` : null;
  if (!key || handled.current === key) return;
  handled.current = key;
  const AGENT_IDS: AgentId[] = ["claude", "codex", "opencode", "qwen"];   // the web AgentId union (types.ts:36)
  const agent = AGENT_IDS.includes(agentParam as AgentId) ? (agentParam as AgentId) : undefined;
  void create({ projectId: projectParam!, ...(agent ? { agent } : {}) }).then((info) => setParams(... delete "project" and "agent", set "focus" ...));
}, [projectParam, agentParam, create, setParams]);
```

## Step-by-step tasks

### UPDATE `apps/graph-manager/src/server/terminals.ts`
- **IMPLEMENT**: `projectId` on `TerminalInfo`, `CreateTerminal`, `Term`, in `create` and `info`; `GM_PROJECT_ID` in `STRIPPED_ENV`. `defaultTitle` is unchanged (the route always passes a title for a project).

### UPDATE `apps/graph-manager/src/server/agents.ts`
- **IMPLEMENT**: `prepareProjectConfig(adapter: AgentAdapter, target: { path: string })`; replace `ws.path` with `target.path`. Drop the `Workspace` import if unused.

### UPDATE `apps/graph-manager/src/server/routes/terminals.ts`
- **IMPLEMENT**: the body field, the both-ids 400, the project branch, title, `projectId` and `GM_PROJECT_ID` for plain and agent terminals, and Qwen's project folder (see Patterns).
- **IMPORTS**: `existsSync` from `node:fs`; `PROJECT_FILE`, `projectDirOf`, `type Project` from `../projects.js`.
- **GOTCHA**: the project folder is inside `workspacesDir`, so `insideWorkspaces` would accept it as a `cwd` too; that path stays as it is (a plain terminal by `cwd` has no `projectId`). Use `path.join` (no `/` literals) for Windows.

### UPDATE `apps/graph-manager/src/server/routes/projects.ts` (DELETE)
- **IMPLEMENT**: also close terminals with `t.projectId === id` (next to the existing cwd check).

### UPDATE `apps/graph-manager/src/server/routes/terminals.test.ts` and `routes/agents.test.ts`
- **IMPLEMENT**:
  - terminals.test.ts (inside the existing `describe.skipIf(win32)`): add a second workspace dir `ws/github/o/s/.git` in the test, `POST /api/projects { name: "billing", workspaces: ["github~o~r", "github~o~s"] }` → 201 (the projects route creates the folder; if `git` needs an identity in CI, the project code already sets one), then `POST /api/terminals { projectId: "billing" }` → 201 `toMatchObject({ projectId: "billing", cwd: path.join(dir, "ws", ".projects", "billing"), title: "billing" })` and no `workspaceId`; `GET /api/terminals` lists it with `projectId`; `{ projectId: "nope" }` → 404 `project not found`; `{ projectId: "billing", workspaceId: "github~o~r" }` → 400; `DELETE /api/projects/billing` → 204 and the terminal is gone from `GET /api/terminals`.
  - agents.test.ts: add `printf 'GM_PROJECT_ID=%s\\n' "$GM_PROJECT_ID";` to the `FAKE` script's recorded lines (keep `GM_TERMINAL_ID` last, since `output()` waits for it). In a new `it`, make a second workspace `github/octo/web` (git init + commit as in `beforeEach`), create the project through `POST /api/projects`, then:
    - `{ projectId: "billing", agent: "claude" }` → 201, title `Claude Code · billing`, `projectId: "billing"`, and the fake records `GM_PROJECT_ID=billing` and `--mcp-config`;
    - `{ projectId: "billing", agent: "qwen" }` → 201 with `connected: { changed: true, commit }`, where `commit` is `git -C <ws>/.projects/billing rev-parse HEAD`, the project repo's last subject is `chore: connect graph-manager tools for Qwen Code`, `<project>/.qwen/settings.json` has the `graph-manager` entry, and the HEAD of `github/octo/hello` and `github/octo/web` did not move; a second call answers `connected: { changed: false }`.
- **PATTERN**: `routes/agents.test.ts:139-162` (Qwen), `routes/terminals.test.ts:73-79`.
- **VALIDATE**: `npm test -w graph-manager -- src/server/routes/terminals src/server/routes/agents src/server/agents src/server/terminals`

### CREATE `apps/graph-manager/src/web/useAgents.ts`; UPDATE `pages/Terminals.tsx`
- **IMPLEMENT**: move `FALLBACK_AGENTS` and `useAgents()` (Terminals.tsx:801–827) unchanged into `src/web/useAgents.ts` and export both; import them back in `Terminals.tsx`. Add `src/web/useProjects.ts`: `export function useProjects(): ProjectEntry[]` — fetches `GET /api/projects` once on mount (`{ projects }`), returns `[]` until it answers and on any error (the existing Terminals tests answer 404 for unknown URLs; they must keep passing).

### UPDATE `apps/graph-manager/src/web/types.ts`
- **IMPLEMENT**: `projectId?: string` on `TerminalInfo` with a doc comment ("set when opened on a project: cwd is the project folder").

### UPDATE `apps/graph-manager/src/web/pages/TerminalSidebar.tsx`
- **IMPLEMENT**: `groupTerminals(terminals, workspaces, projects: { id: string; name: string }[] = [])`: after the workspace sections, one section per project with terminals (key `project:<id>`, label = the project's name, else the id; in the order of `projects`, unknown ids last), then "Workspaces root" for terminals with neither `workspaceId` nor `projectId`. `shownOrder` and `TerminalSidebarProps` take the same optional `projects`. The section header gets a small `Icon name="projects"` (it exists in `ui/Icon.tsx` since the projects task; if not, use `folder`).

### UPDATE `apps/graph-manager/src/web/pages/Terminals.tsx`
- **IMPLEMENT**:
  - `const projects = useProjects();` pass it to `TerminalSidebar` and `shownOrder`.
  - `NewTerminalBody = { workspaceId?: string; projectId?: string; title?: string; agent?: AgentId }`.
  - The `?project=<id>[&agent=<agentId>]` effect (Patterns). An unknown agent id is ignored (plain terminal). Errors show in the page's error bar like `?workspace=` today.
  - `NewTerminalDialog`: add a `projects` prop; after the workspace `<option>`s add `<optgroup label="Projects">` with `<option value={\`project:${p.id}\`}>{p.name}</option>` (only when there are projects). On submit, a value starting with `project:` sends `{ projectId }` instead of `{ workspaceId }`. For Qwen (`needsWorkspace`), a project counts as a workspace; change the hint to "Commits .qwen/settings.json once (in the workspace or project folder) if graph-manager's tools are not connected yet." only if no test asserts the old full text (`Terminals.test.tsx:507` checks `toContain("Commits .qwen/settings.json once")`, which still matches).
- **GOTCHA**: `?project=` must use its own `handled` ref (not the `?workspace=` one). Keep the workspaces first in the select: the Qwen test expects the first workspace to be preselected (`Terminals.test.tsx:506-507`). Spec watching, run chips and `itemWorkspace` stay keyed on `workspaceId`; a project terminal simply has none (later work).

### UPDATE `apps/graph-manager/src/web/pages/Projects.tsx` (+ `Projects.css`)
- **IMPLEMENT**: in each row's actions cell, before **Edit repos**, a `div.pj-agents` (`role="group"`, `aria-label="Open a terminal on <name>"`) with one icon button per agent from `useAgents()`: `className="btn btn-sm btn-icon pj-agent"`, `<AgentIcon agent={a.id} />`, `aria-label={\`Open ${a.label} on ${p.name}\`}`, `title` the same (or `${a.binary} is not installed`), `disabled={!a.installed}`, `data-testid={\`project-agent-${p.id}-${a.id}\`}`, navigating to `/terminals?project=<id>&agent=<a.id>`; and a plain button `Icon terminal` + "Terminal" (`data-testid={\`project-terminal-${p.id}\`}`) to `/terminals?project=<id>`. Use `encodeURIComponent`. CSS: tokens only, keep the row on one line above 900px; under 900px the buttons may wrap.
- **PATTERN**: `pages/TerminalSidebar.tsx:78-102` (the agent buttons), `pages/Workspaces.tsx:225-228` (the Open terminal link).

### UPDATE `apps/graph-manager/src/web/pages/Terminals.test.tsx` and `pages/Projects.test.tsx`
- **IMPLEMENT**:
  - Terminals: let `serve()` answer `GET /api/projects` with `{ projects: [BILLING] }` (`BILLING = { id: "billing", name: "billing", forge: "github", path: "/ws/.projects/billing", createdAt: ago(60), workspaces: [...] }`) and keep `projectId` from the POST body in the created terminal.
    - a terminal with `projectId: "billing"` shows in `section-project:billing` labelled `billing`, after the workspace sections and before `section-root`;
    - `/terminals?project=billing&agent=claude` in StrictMode POSTs once `{ projectId: "billing", agent: "claude" }` and becomes `?focus=<id>`; `?project=billing` alone POSTs `{ projectId: "billing" }`;
    - the New terminal dialog lists `billing` under "Projects" and Create with it selected POSTs `{ projectId: "billing" }`.
  - Projects: each row shows the agent buttons; one whose CLI is not installed is disabled; clicking Claude Code navigates to `/terminals?project=billing&agent=claude`; the plain Terminal button to `/terminals?project=billing`.
- **VALIDATE**: `npm test -w graph-manager -- src/web/pages/Terminals src/web/pages/Projects`

## Look at it in a browser (TESTING.md: UI changes must be seen)

Start graph-manager as in TESTING.md "graph-manager" (temp dirs, free port). Make two workspaces (`for r in github/octo/api github/octo/web; do mkdir -p $GM_DIR/ws/$r && git -C $GM_DIR/ws/$r init -q -b main; done`) and a project: `curl -s -b $GM_DIR/c -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"name":"billing","workspaces":["github~octo~api","github~octo~web"]}' http://127.0.0.1:<port>/api/projects`. With `agent-browser`: open **Projects**, press the plain **Terminal** button on `billing`: the Terminals page opens a terminal titled `billing` in a `billing` sidebar section; type `pwd; ls repos; echo $GM_PROJECT_ID` → the `.projects/billing` folder, `api web`, `billing`. If `claude` is installed, the Claude Code button opens `Claude Code · billing` (otherwise check that it is disabled with "claude is not installed"). Take screenshots and read them; report their paths.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `POST /api/terminals { projectId }` → 201 with `cwd` = `<workspacesDir>/.projects/<id>`, `title` = the project name (`<Agent> · <name>` for an agent), `projectId`, no `workspaceId`; the shell's env has `GM_PROJECT_ID=<id>` (also after a restart); unknown id → 404 `project not found`; with `workspaceId` too → 400.
- [ ] Agent buttons work on a project; Qwen Code's `.qwen/settings.json` is committed in the project folder's repo, never in a workspace.
- [ ] Deleting a project closes its terminals.
- [ ] Terminals page: a sidebar section per project; `?project=<id>[&agent=<id>]` opens one terminal (StrictMode-safe) and becomes `?focus=`; the New terminal dialog offers projects.
- [ ] Projects page: per-project agent buttons and a plain Terminal button open terminals on the project; uninstalled agents are disabled.
- [ ] The new tests exist and pass; all existing graph-manager tests (Terminals, agents, terminals routes) still pass.

npm run typecheck && npm run lint
npm test -w graph-manager -- src/server/routes/terminals src/server/routes/agents src/server/agents src/server/terminals src/server/routes/projects

npm test -w graph-manager
